name: French Raspberry
lede: French Raspberry is a deep, slightly crimson red named for France and the fruit raspberry, rare in our archive.

sections.title: A place word on a fruit color
sections.body: French Raspberry pairs the place word "French" with [[raspberry]], the fruit's color [1]. Wikipedia's color list again credits the French site Pourpre.com as its source; the deeper origin of the pairing is not documented in our data [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[lipstick]], [[carmine-m-p]] and [[brick-red]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this red in 0.04 percent of the 23,781 paintings we have, 9 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 6 [2]. That makes it rarer than 73 percent of the named colors in our archive, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match in our archive is from 1800; the archive's early centuries are thin, so with so few paintings this is a floor, not a first [2]. Among our French-named siblings, [[french-fuchsia]] and [[french-sky-blue]] follow the same pattern: a place word in front of an existing color word, traced to Pourpre.com, with little trace in painting [2].
